rows: An African Blue Flycatcher
This small bird has bright blue feathers and a long tail with a crest on its head. It lives in the forests of central Africa. Giles Laurent photographed it in Uganda's Kibale National Park.

A Chimpanzee in Kibale
An alpha male chimpanzee sits quietly in the forest, looking at the camera. Chimpanzees are one of our closest living relatives and share about 98 percent of our DNA.

The Pillars of Creation, Seen by Webb
In 2022 the James Webb Space Telescope looked at the Pillars of Creation in near-infrared light, which can see through dust. The red dots at the tips are baby stars just beginning to form.
How is this different from the Hubble pictures of the same pillars?
The Cosmic Cliffs

On July 12, 2022, NASA shared Webb's first full-color images. The Cosmic Cliffs are the edge of a huge cloud of gas in the Carina Nebula where stars are forming. The mountains and valleys seem to glow, though the tallest peaks are about seven light-years high.
How can gas clouds look like mountains?
The Southern Ring Nebula

A dying star at the center has puffed off layers of gas. Webb photographed it in two different kinds of infrared light, on the left with its near-infrared camera and on the right with its mid-infrared one, and the images show different details.
Which picture shows more of the central stars?
A Sea Slug
This nudibranch, or sea slug, wears bright blue and purple colors to warn predators that it tastes bad. Many sea slugs get chemicals from the sponges they eat and use them as defense.
Why would a snail without a shell have such bright colors?
Córdoba, Spain

The Roman Bridge crosses the Guadalquivir River in Córdoba, with the city's great cathedral behind it. The cathedral began as a mosque more than a thousand years ago, and still has hundreds of red-and-white arches inside.

The Andromeda Galaxy, Amateur Photo

The Andromeda Galaxy can be seen with the naked eye on a dark night, but a long exposure shows its swirling arms. Amateurs now make photographs of galaxies that would have needed observatories in the past.

Grotto in an Iceberg

Herbert Ponting was the photographer on Captain Scott's Terra Nova expedition to Antarctica. He photographed a member of the team standing in a blue ice cave in an iceberg. Ponting was the first professional photographer to work in Antarctica.

The Church of St. John at Kaneo
A small stone church stands on a cliff above Lake Ohrid, in North Macedonia. It was built in the 1200s, and the water below is among the deepest and oldest lakes in Europe.

A Stingless Bee Nest
A round nest hangs among the leaves of a tree. Stingless bees live in many warm countries, making honey and wax but, as their name says, not stinging.

The Green Comet
Comet C/2022 E3 (ZTF) glows green because its gas contains carbon molecules that shine in sunlight. It passed close to Earth in early 2023, for the first time in about 50,000 years.

A Flying Fox in Flight
A Polynesian flying fox, a kind of fruit bat, spreads its wings against a blue sky. With wings that can span almost a meter, it flies at night to eat fruit and spreads seeds.

The Petzval Lens

In 1840, the Viennese mathematician Joseph Petzval designed a lens by calculation, making it about twenty times faster than earlier ones. Portrait exposures dropped from minutes to seconds, and Voigtländer made the brass lens in this photograph.
Why was a faster lens such a big change for portraits?
Earthset from Orion

Earth, a bright crescent of blue, sets behind the horizon of the Moon, photographed from NASA's Orion spacecraft in 2026. Like the Earthrise pictures of Apollo, it shows how our planet looks from the Moon.
